newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Insurance fund to seek bank loans in June.
newsitem.headline: Japan Insurance fund to seek bank loans in June.

text.p: The semi-governmental Deposit Insurance Corp of Japan (DIC) said on Monday that it would seek loans worth about 440 billion yen from banks through a tender in June that will be the first of its kind.
The move is aimed at repaying stop-gap loans provided by the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to the insurance group, a Deposit Insurance Corp official said.
Japan's deposit insurance system, set up in 1971, is designed to help prevent a financial crisis and protect depositors from any financial failures.

The DIC has borrowed about 540 billion yen from the central bank to help pay 1.03 trillion yen to a liquidation scheme for failed credit union Kizu Shinyo Kumiai and to provide 26.2 billion yen to another liquidation scheme for failed Sanpuku Shinyo Kumiai.

The official said that the tender would take place in June, when financial institutions make their half-yearly deposit insurance premium payments, which will cover some 100 billion yen of the BOJ loans.
He said that details of the tender have not yet been worked out, but the term for the bank loans would be set at six months and would be rolled over.
In the tender, which would not be mandatory, banks would indicate interest rates on loans and the DIC would select those with lower rates, financial industry sources said.

The DIC was dormant until 1992, but it has used a total of 2.08 trillion yen in the past five years to bail out troubled financial institutions and to cover losses stemming from a series of financial failures since 1995.
The sources said there are worries that the funds available in the deposit insurance system may not be enough to protect depositors, and the DIC may boost the insurance premiums again.

Under financial bills passed by parliament last June aimed at solving Japan's problem loan mess, the DIC boosted the insurance premiums which financial institutions pay by seven times, to 0.084 percent of total deposits from 0.012 percent.
This means the DIC will get 500 billion yen in premiums a year until 2001, the DIC official said. The DIC can also borrow a total of two trillion yen from the central bank as stop-gap funds.
Under the financial bills, the premium could be reviewed in March 1999, he said.
